**22 palavras novas** (problemas sociais).

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo integrar leitura, escuta, fala e escrita sobre um aviso comunitário e usar o phrasal verb rule something out.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Neighborhood Meeting: Who Is Responsible for the Park?
lines: The park has become a source of tension. **It is reported that** litter, noise and parking are the main complaints. The council **has not ruled out** closing it at night, but it **has ruled out** private security for now.

We **suggest that** each resident **attend** and that the council **explain** its plans. **It is essential that** every group **be** represented. Bring your ideas: **the more voices**, **the better** the plan.

items.q: The council has ruled out closing the park at night.
The council has ruled out private security.
Only residents who complain should attend.

blocks.body: **rule out** é separável: *rule out the idea* / *rule the idea out* / *rule it out* (✗ *rule out it*). Na passiva: *The option has been ruled out.*

items.s: The council has ___ out private security. (rule)
It is essential that every group ___ represented. (be)

prompts.q: Make a suggestion with the subjunctive.
prompts.model: I suggest that each group attend.
It is reported that litter is the main complaint.

blocks.task: Write a flyer (6 sentences) inviting residents to a meeting, using rule out, a subjunctive and the more…, the better.
blocks.model: Neighborhood Meeting: Our Park. It is reported that litter is a growing problem. The council has not ruled out new rules. We suggest that every resident attend. It is essential that all views be heard. The more voices, the better the decision.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
